facts.fact: Maintaining the weight and balance records
The pilot in command is responsible for knowing the maximum allowable weight and CG limits before each flight.
Higher takeoff speed and a longer takeoff run.
Reduced rate and angle of climb.
Reduced cruising speed and shorter range.
A deliberate attempt to load the aircraft for the most critical balance condition.
Needed when the new EWCG falls outside the EWCG range.
Too far aft: unstable and difficult to recover from a stall.
Too far forward: insufficient elevator authority to rotate or flare.
Weight acts through the single wing attach point.
The range is fixed, so no calculated range is needed.
Unsecured dogs moved aft during takeoff.
Unsecured skydivers seated toward the aft.
The average of the root chord and the tip chord.
2 at 143.5 inches and 2 at 180 inches aft of datum.
The moment is divided by 1,000 to make it more manageable.
After extensive repair or major alteration.
When the pilot reports unsatisfactory flight characteristics.
When recorded data are suspected to be in error.
Not below 40 °F or above 100 °F unless designed for it.
Drain until the gauges read empty in level-flight attitude.
Residual fuel is part of empty weight.
Tare is the weight of the chocks.
Subtract it from the scale reading to get net weight.
13.2 inches forward of the main-wheel weighing points.
Add and remove a weight, then recheck zero.
Repeat until a steady zero is obtained.
The moment divided by a reduction factor such as 100 or 1,000.
Empty weight arm and/or moment index.
Lead bars or canvas bags of sand or lead shot.
Marked 'Ballast XX Pounds—Removal Requires Weight and Balance Check'.
Fixed-wing aircraft above 12,500 pounds takeoff weight.
If more than 36 calendar months since the last weighing.
Or if a modification warrants it.
CG 909.6 inches aft of the datum.
Basic or fleet empty weight plus operational items.
Empty weight plus required crew and their baggage.
Plus standard items such as meals and potable water.
Standard empty weight plus optional equipment.
Permanent ballast is part of empty weight.
Temporary ballast must be removed when weighed.
The CG moves forward when fuel is used from the outboard tanks.
The datum is 100 inches in front of the forward face of the firewall bulkhead.
Potable water is not part of empty weight.
Lavatory precharge water is not part of empty weight.
Water for injection into the engines is not part of empty weight.
Minimum fuel is the fuel needed for half an hour at rated maximum continuous power.
In pounds it is METO horsepower divided by 2.
Permanent ballast is usually lead blocks painted red.
It is marked "Permanent Ballast—Do Not Remove".
It is attached so it cannot be dislodged and does not interfere with control action.
When the cumulative weight change exceeds ±0.5% of the maximum landing weight.
Or when the cumulative CG change exceeds 0.5% of the MAC.
It is within the envelope for takeoff.
It is 77 lb over the 2,950 lb maximum landing weight.
About 77 lb of fuel must be burned before landing.
-O marks optional equipment items replacing required or standard items.
A full 5-gallon tank lasts about 9 hours.
It shuts down when coolant temperature exceeds 225 ± 5 °F (107 ± 3 °C).
The restriction indicator on the air cleaner housing displays red.
DC CONTROL POWER circuit breaker pushed in.
Crank no more than 15 seconds at a time.
Wait at least 15 seconds between attempts.
AC CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER switch to OPEN.
Run five minutes with no load.
DEAD CRANK switch to OFF after the After Operation PMCS.
Below 40 °F, use PREHEAT for at most 30 seconds before cranking.
Check and service a dirty air cleaner element and fuel filter/water separator.
Hold the MASTER SWITCH in START until oil pressure reaches 25 psi.
Check the FAULT INDICATOR lights (NO FUEL: paragraph 3-3.5.1; other lights: notify the next maintenance level).
Check the circuit breaker on the side of the Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter and reset it if tripped.
A wing nut (item 16) holds the filter element.
Protected by a Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter.
And an overload circuit breaker inside the control box.
The fan belt drives the alternator.
The alternator is rated 18 amps at 24 VDC.
The transfer pump draws fuel from the tank.
Fuel passes through the fuel filter/water separator.
Injection pumps pressurize it into the injectors.
Unused fuel returns through an excess fuel return line.
MASTER SWITCH on PRIME & RUN AUX FUEL runs the auxiliary pump.
The pump transfers fuel from the external supply.
The float switch shuts the pump off when the tank is full and restarts it as the level drops.
Two preheaters warm the air intake manifold.
They work with the MASTER SWITCH in PREHEAT.
The magnetic pickup senses engine speed.
The crank disconnect switch opens and de-energizes the cranking relay.
No other starting or control function is activated.
Load can be applied immediately if required.
MASTER SWITCH to PRIME AND RUN.
Press PRESS TO TEST; all lights should light and go out when released.
Rotate the AM-VM switch through each phase while watching the ammeter.
Reduce load if any phase shows more than rated load.
Load lines to L1, L2 and L3.
In the holding clip on the right side of the skid base.
